To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
social networking sites (SNS) use is positively related with the development of social capital among overseas students.
social searching on social networking sites (SNS) positively predicted the amount in bridging social capital among students in new environment.
SNS use is positively associated with social capital, which in turn is positively associated with adjustment to life transition in a new environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of social capital in SNS use, psychological well-being and life transition.
the impact of SNS use on social capital and psychological adjustment during life transition.
the impact of social media on social capital and life satisfaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SNS use and social capital of the students are closely related, which in turn affects the psychological well-being of these students.
SNS use is an important factor for students to adjust to life transition.
social capital is a key factor to explain the impact of SNS use on psychological well-being.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

social searching and public interaction on SNS are positively associated with bridging social capital, which in turn positively predicted life satisfaction among overseas Chinese students in Hong Kong.
SNS use is a double-edged sword in terms of its impact on psychological well-being.
SNS can be used to build up social capital for overseas students.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SNS is an important tool for overseas students to connect with others and build up social capital in new environment.
SNS use can facilitate social capital development, which in turn can enhance psychological well-being.
social capital is a critical factor in the relationship between SNS use and life satisfaction.
